title: Introduce hemisphere fencing and eviction softening to reduce cross-region thrash
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: during recent regional flapping episodes we observed coordinated tenant evictions and rapid cross-region failovers that amplified SLO violations. This PR implements a hemisphere fencing layer (a soft region boundary) that biases new tenant admission and eviction decisions to prefer local capacity while allowing controlled, metric-driven cross-hemisphere fallback. Key goals are to reduce cascading evictions, smooth SLO enforcement, and avoid mass KV-cache thrash. Summary of changes: 1) routing/hemisphere_fence.go: new admission policy that tracks per-hemisphere free_slots and recent eviction_rate and applies a dampened admission factor; 2) slo/enforcer.py: when eviction pressure exceeds threshold, apply 'eviction softening' which increases tenant quiesce windows and lowers eviction aggressiveness for low-priority classes; 3) scheduler/priority_gate.cc: add a lightweight probe annealing backoff to avoid rapid open/close cycles on circuit breakers; 4) autoscale/policy.yaml: updated defaults to prefer same-hemisphere scale-up before cross-hemisphere routing; 5) docs/ops/hemisphere-fencing.md: operational runbook; 6) tests/hemisphere_fence_test.go and workload simulations to validate behavior under synthetic flaps. Hotfix rationale: this was reverted once in the field to mitigate a regression where very small tenants were never admitted — addressed here with minimum admission floor and additional unit tests. Backwards compatibility: changes are opt-in by default via env var REDWOOD_HEMISPHERE_FENCE=enabled and new config flag enable_eviction_softening; default remains conservative. Rollout plan: staged canary on three zones, monitor SLO error budget burn and eviction rate, gradually enable across regions over 48 hours. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration simulation, [x] manual canary run, [x] docs updated. Testing notes: synthetic traffic harness shows 28% fewer simultaneous evictions at peak and 12% lower 99th-percentile tail latency on affected routes. Related: references ENG-2145 (regional stability) and SUP-9987 support ticket from customer incident. Merge notes: squash-merged to main after CI rerun. Revert/rollback: disable env var and/or revert flag to restore previous behavior.
